about: Every route's ceilings, the one table (17 Oct 2026; the coordinator's rule: one source of route ceilings). A line for every page and layout under app/.

source: bytes of source the file reaches by static import (a dynamic import() is a chunk of its own and isn't followed), measured by scripts/fluidity/reach.mjs and held by app/firstLoad.test.ts on every quick check, with no build. A layout's line is the layout's own reach; a page's leaves its layouts out.

gzipKB: a page's first-load script in a production build, gzip -9, with the runtime and every layout above it, measured and held by scripts/fluidity/routes.mjs --check after the build (the integrator's full gate).
beyondHome: the doc route's source beyond Home's, as app/app/doc/docFirstLoad.test.ts has held it since 12 Oct (docs A1).

Both only ever go down. A new page needs its line before its first gate (routes.mjs --propose prints it); a route over its line makes what it brings lazy (next/dynamic, import()) rather than raising it. Lower a line when a change brings its route down.

The room rule (coordinator, 18 Oct 2026): a source line is its route's measure plus 2 KB (2,000 bytes), rounded up to the next 1,000. It applies to a new route's first line and to a line lowered after its route shrinks, and a line never rises above its own established value except through this rule. A gzip line is its measure plus 1.5%, rounded up to the next KB. The lines first set at their exact measure on 17-18 Oct took this room once, on 18 Oct (the tables list, 634,842 to 637,000 and 491 to 499 KB), and the invitation page's first line is 121,000 by it (measured 118,009); design/docs-vs-notion/INTEGRATION.md lists them.
edition: "ai" marks a page only the AI edition has; the edition without AI keeps the line and has no page for it.

target, where a programme set one, is where the route must get to, and owner the package that gets it there. New lines were set on 17 Oct at the measure plus 1.5%, after the shell diet (platform P-SPEED: Home 637 to 575 KB, sign-up 381 to 309); the four that existed kept their values.

The call routes (meet ch, chat, grp, m and instant, and the guest's call page) were set again on 18 Oct from P-SPEED merged with CALLS-1, at the measure plus 1.5% (meet/ch 982,277 bytes of source): CALLS-1 adds about 47 KB to each, which CALLS-4 makes lazy (the People panel's host tools, the person and co-host menus, the lock), and CALLS-4 lowers these lines when it lands. Their gzip lines held with CALLS-1 merged (meet/ch 669 KB).

The calendar event page was set again on 18 Oct from P-SPEED merged with beta b18i2 (863d605ef), at the measure plus 1.5%: CAL-A7's repeating events had added about 63 KB of source to it (890,664 bytes, 575 KB gzip), and calendar A2's guests and answers then 54 KB more (944,456 bytes of source). CAL-LEAD lowered it the same day (cal-lazy): the repeat editor, the scope question, Tell guests? and the assistant's Find a better time and Prep brief load when the page is idle or on first use, as the grid's do. With A2, 808,300 bytes of source and 566 KB gzip. The source line is the measure with calendar A5 merged as well (its reminders row behind the same boundary), 810,992 bytes, rounded up to the next 1,000 (the rule since 03:50 on 18 Oct); the gzip line is the measure plus 1.5%. The invitation page (A2) has its first lines from the same build, by the same rules: 118,009 bytes of source (line 119,000) and 235 KB gzip (line 239). The one Event Form (calendar FORM) then took the panel's inline edit form off the page (747,262 bytes of source), and its edit kit (the form's values, the notes' conversions and the save) went behind the same boundary with DESIGN-BUILD-2's review: 726,013 bytes with calendar A5's review merged, so its line is 729,000 (the measure plus 2 KB, rounded up: the rule since 10:25 on 18 Oct for a route a package shrinks); its gzip line, from the same build (515 KB), is the measure plus 1.5%: 523.
